docs.overviewBody: The marketplace lists communication (Outlook, Gmail), repository (GitHub), API-key MCP servers, and vendor-hosted remote MCP integrations. Connected integrations appear under Connected and on the MCP tab when they expose tools to agents.
docs.remoteMcpBody: Official providers (Notion, Linear, Slack, and others) host their own MCP server. Bokito starts OAuth in the browser, stores tokens per workspace, and agents receive a bearer token when calling vendor tools.
docs.remoteMcpStep1: Open Marketplace, filter MCP, and choose a provider.
docs.remoteMcpStep2: Select Set up connection and complete OAuth at the vendor.
docs.remoteMcpStep3: Verify the connection under Connected or MCP servers.
docs.catalogHint: Cards marked Coming soon need platform OAuth configuration before connect is available.
docs.existingGithub: GitHub repository indexing uses a separate OAuth flow (not the GitHub MCP card).
docs.existingInbox: Outlook and Gmail use inbox OAuth; mailboxes are managed under Settings.
docs.existingApiKeyMcp: Bjorn Lunden MCP and Custom MCP use an API key or URL instead of remote OAuth.
docs.adminBody: Remote MCP requires the integrations API patches, runtime OAuth service, and per-vendor OAuth apps. Until configured, providers stay in Coming soon status.
docs.devBody: Technical setup guides live in the GitHub repository for engineers deploying Xano and runtime:
